findings.what: The stage says it makes two behavior changes. We measured a third. When the Rails log is switched on (LOGGING_RAILS_LOG_ENABLED=true; off by default, on in config/examples/development.yml, and one of the seven boot configurations the stage checks), the line Rails writes for every request changes shape. On 7.1.6: 'Completed 200 OK in 39ms (Views: 26.1ms | ActiveRecord: 1.4ms | Allocations: 22156)'. On 7.2.4: 'Completed 200 OK in 39ms (Views: 23.2ms | ActiveRecord: 1.1ms (1 query, 0 cached) | GC: 13.1ms)'. The 'Rendered ...' lines change the same way at the end ('Allocations: N' becomes 'GC: N ms'). The query count is in the Action View 7.2 changelog as 'Add queries count to template rendering instrumentation' (https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v7.2.4/actionview/CHANGELOG.md). The replacement of 'Allocations' by 'GC' is in none of the seven changelogs we read; the changelog's own example still shows 'Allocations'. We found it by diffing the two installed versions and then running 52 production requests on each: 280 log lines on each side, of which all 46 'Completed' lines and all 24 'Rendered' lines differ in this way and no other line differs (times and ids masked). No check could have shown it: the boot check starts the application with the Rails log on and does not read what it writes. The application's own request log (config/initializers/logging.rb, the one that is on by default) is the same on both versions; we compared it. No application code is wrong and the impact is small. It matters to anyone who feeds the Rails log to a parser, a dashboard or an alert that reads the 'Completed' line beyond the status. What has to change is text: declare the difference with its source, make the count of declared changes three, and add a follow-up asking the client whether anything reads those lines.
findings.where: exec/stages/S3/notes.md and pr-body.md, 'Declared behavior changes' (source: actionpack 7.2.4 lib/action_controller/log_subscriber.rb and activerecord 7.2.4 lib/active_record/railties/controller_runtime.rb)

findings.what: Carried from all three earlier reviews, still open: json is not pinned below 3 in the Gemfile, and the plan put the pin in S2. Active Support 7.2 and 8.0 pass an option that json 3 removed. The lock holds json 2.7.1 and JSON encoding works on 7.2.4 (probe). The only thing holding json below 3 is rubocop 1.48.1 in the development group, which requires json ~> 2.3 (Gemfile.lock:348). That protection goes when rubocop is upgraded. Belongs to S2's follow-up or to S4 before its relock. The notes list it as a follow-up.

The third review's defect is fixed, and we confirmed it. The HEAD difference is declared with its source, and the three new examples fail on 7.1.6 exactly as the notes say (2 of 3, on Content-Type and Content-Length). The notes say the 500 page was read and not measured; we measured it. GET is identical on both versions. HEAD behaves as declared: Content-Length 1477 on 7.1.6 and 0 on 7.2.4, Content-Type '*/*' on 7.2.4 for 'Accept: */*'. The same holds for a 406 and for a 404 raised by a missing record. The author can change 'read, not measured' to 'measured'. Earlier fixes also hold: with the migration waiter fix reverted 2 of 4 examples fail, and the lock differs from S2 only in what the stage lists.

Two things a developer will meet, neither a change in what the application does. First, db/schema.rb still says 'ActiveRecord::Schema[7.1]'. Rails 7.2.4 loads it without complaint, and the next time someone runs a migration in development Rails rewrites that line to '[7.2]' and drops the blank line before the final 'end'. That is a two-line diff with no schema change; we redid all 12 versioned migrations on both versions and the tables come out identical. Second, building a database by running every migration from nothing fails on both versions, because 7 migrations from 2016 and 2017 inherit from ActiveRecord::Migration without a version. This is older than the upgrade and the same before and after; new installs load the schema instead (rake postal:update), which works on 7.2.4.

Rollback is safe for signed-in users, which nobody had measured. With the same secret key, cookies issued on 7.2.4 are accepted on 7.1.6 and cookies issued on 7.1.6 are accepted on 7.2.4: the user stays signed in and a form post with a CSRF token from the other version's session is accepted. The stage's session continuity spec covers the forward direction only.

Still open from earlier reviews, and the notes say so: the author did not run bin/rails app:update (the rake form of that task no longer exists on 7.2.4; the bin/rails form does); the client has column names for stored 'Astana' values but no query; the seventh change under S3 in out/plan.json still asks for the withdrawn secret key declaration; app/models/route.rb:119 copies a nil error message, the same before and after this stage.

method.changelogs_not_read: actioncable, actionmailbox, actiontext, activejob and activestorage for 7.2 were not read: config/application.rb requires six railties and none of these five is among them (inventory.json, framework_config). We read the other seven files from top to bottom. We counted the entries ourselves in four of them (actionpack 36, actionview 25, activemodel 6, actionmailer 4, 'No changes' placeholders left out); for activerecord, activesupport and railties we took the counts from the third review's record of the same files. Entries that apply: the soft deprecation of ActiveRecord::Base.connection (lib/tasks/postal.rake:31, runs, prints nothing); the Astana zone (declared; we diffed the two installed time_zone.rb files and Astana is the only name whose mapping moved); the 7.2.3 secret_key_base entry (checked, no change, as the notes say); show_exceptions true/false removed (changed in test.rb); the Rack 3.2 :unprocessable_entity conversion (422 responses identical on both versions; the Ruby warning 7.1.6 prints is gone); the HEAD entry for PublicExceptions (declared; measured again on 404, 406 and now 500); the Action View entry 'Add queries count to template rendering instrumentation' (finding 1: it changes the Rails request log line, and the stage does not declare it); the HAML capture fix (50 production responses and the 170 recorded ones show no difference from it). Entries we chased and found not to apply: the 7.2.4 UnknownHttpMethod fix (an unknown method answers 405 on both versions here); has_secure_password confirmation on blank (the application calls it with validations: false and has its own confirmation rule, has_authentication.rb:8-11); 'Request Forgery takes relative paths into account' (the installed 7.1.6 and 7.2.4 request_forgery_protection.rb differ in one unrelated line, and real tokens from real forms verify on both); the scientific notation change in the number helpers (the views pass numbers, not strings); Inflector.humanize (the status names it is called on are ASCII); 'Support the RETURNING clause for MariaDB' (the sandbox database is MariaDB 10.11 and reports insert returning as supported, so the suite ran on that path). We searched repo/ for the removed and renamed connection, pool, serialize, enum, deprecation, secrets and tag helper names and found no use beyond lib/tasks/postal.rake:31. We did not repeat the third review's search of 23 gems that hook into Rails; the lock for those gems is unchanged since then.

upstream_diff.why_not: We read every patch in upstream.json (two patches there are cut short by the recorder: the removed 7.0 defaults file and the added 7.1 defaults file) and every row of answer_key.json. None of the 11 files is a break this stage needed. The explicit YAML coder on the two serialized columns: under load_defaults 7.0 both columns already resolve to the YAML coder on 7.2.4 and round trip (probe). Replacing dynamic_form: their choice; its error list renders the same HTML on 7.1.6 and 7.2.4 in production (the invalid settings form, byte for byte apart from the Astana line). The framework defaults files belong to the config stage. db/schema.rb: their change is for 8.1; we note that 7.2.4 would write 'Schema[7.2]' and drop the trailing blank line the next time a developer migrates (finding 4). The annotate rake files belong to S2 and the 8.1 hop. lib/migration_waiter.rb and config/environments/test.rb carry the same change on both sides. Their Gemfile pins json below 3 and this one does not (finding 2). Their work mentions neither the HEAD difference nor the request log difference.
